close_reason: Changed cert_sha256_of return type from [u8; 32] to Option<[u8; 32]>, propagating None on DER encode failure. Eliminates false equality of SHA256(empty)=e3b0c4... across distinct un-encodable certs. Existing test run_cert_stamps_cert_sha256_on_findings exercises the Some(_) happy path; encode-failure path enforced at type level (downstream Finding.cert_sha256 was already Option<[u8;32]>). All 124 lib tests pass, clippy --all-features clean.
description: Trigger: load a Certificate that successfully decodes from DER but fails to re-encode (e.g., a Certificate containing a field x509-cert can decode but cannot round-trip through Encode — this is rare but not theoretical, since x509-cert's encoders can fail on edge cases the decoders accept). cert_sha256_of (lib.rs:145-156) catches the encode error with .unwrap_or_default() and proceeds to hash an empty Vec, producing SHA256(empty) = e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855. Actual bad behavior: every finding produced by run_cert on this cert is stamped with the same well-known empty-input hash, making evidence packs claim provenance for a cert whose content cannot be reproduced. Two distinct broken certs produce findings with the same cert_sha256. The comment says 'malformed Certificate would have failed to parse before reaching this function' — but the function takes &Certificate, which is constructed by the parser. x509-cert's roundtrip is documented to occasionally fail (DEFAULT-tagged fields, BMPString edge cases). Fix: change Vec<Finding> to surface the encode failure as a Fatal finding, or use a non-default sentinel (Option<[u8;32]>) so consumers can distinguish 'this cert failed to encode' from 'this cert had a meaningful all-zero hash.' Either way the silent fallback to SHA256(empty) is wrong.
title: cert_sha256_of swallows DER encode error, stamps all-zero hash on findings
